events.title: Karl Marx is born in Trier
events.description: The philosopher and economist was born in Trier, in the Kingdom of Prussia. He grew up to co-author The Communist Manifesto with Friedrich Engels and to write Das Kapital.
events.significance: His ideas about class, labor and capitalism shaped political movements, revolutions and the social sciences throughout the 19th and 20th centuries.

events.title: Napoleon Bonaparte dies on Saint Helena
events.description: The former French emperor died in exile on the remote South Atlantic island of Saint Helena. He had been held there by the British after his defeat at Waterloo in 1815.
events.significance: His death closed the Napoleonic era. His legal reforms, military legacy and myth continued to influence Europe long afterward.

events.title: Mexican forces win the Battle of Puebla
events.description: A smaller Mexican army under General Ignacio Zaragoza defeated French troops near the city of Puebla. The French army was considered among the best in the world at the time.
events.significance: The victory became a lasting symbol of Mexican resistance and national pride. It is the origin of the Cinco de Mayo commemorations.

events.title: Alan Shepard becomes the first American in space
events.description: Astronaut Alan Shepard flew aboard Freedom 7 on a suborbital flight of about 15 minutes. It was launched from Cape Canaveral, Florida.
events.significance: The flight came weeks after the Soviet Union's Yuri Gagarin orbited Earth. It was a key early step in the American space program and helped lead to the Moon landings.
